subject: Urban Planning
title: Resilience Planning: Designing for the Worst
description: A quick, practical guide to Resilience Planning: Designing for the Worst.

hook.text: Tokyo built its first earthquake-resistant buildings in 1923 after the Great Kanto Earthquake killed 140,000 people.

buildup.text: Japan's building codes now require base isolation — buildings float on rubber pads that absorb earthquake energy.

discovery.text: The 2011 Tōhoku earthquake was magnitude 9.0. Almost no buildings collapsed. The codes worked perfectly.

twist.text: The tsunami killed 20,000 people because seawalls were too low. Engineering can't predict every scenario.

climax.text: Resilience planning now includes retreat — moving people away from danger zones instead of building walls.

punchline.text: Prepare for disaster. Accept you can't prevent every one.

quiz.question: What is 'base isolation' in earthquake-resistant building design?
options: Building foundations deep underground into bedrock
Placing buildings on rubber pads that absorb earthquake energy
Constructing buildings with flexible steel frames that sway
